classification.classification_note: The observed memory error is a heap out-of-bounds read through a one-past-end `struct generic_shdr *`. The underlying coding error is an off-by-one upper-bound check on section numbers read from an `SHT_GROUP` payload.

bug_description.original: A test for a section group section-reference in src/lib/libdwarf/dwarf_elf_load_headers.c fails to catch a section number that is just one too big, potentially allowing out-of-bounds section references.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 1961-byte `poc` is a corrupted ELF64 big-endian object. Static inspection shows `e_shnum == 4`, and section header 1 is an `SHT_GROUP` section with `sh_offset == 0x64`, `sh_size == 0x0f`, and `sh_entsize == 4`. `generic_ehdr_from_64()` copies `e_shnum` into `ehdr->ge_shnum`, `generic_shdr_from_shdr64()` allocates a 4-element `generic_shdr` array, and `_dwarf_elf_setup_all_section_groups()` dispatches section 1 to `read_gs_section_group()`. The first group-member bytes after the 32-bit flag are `04 00 00 00`, so `read_gs_section_group()` materializes `gseca == 4` while `ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count == 4`. The vulnerable checks `if (gseca > ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count)` and `if (gsecb > ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count)` reject only strictly larger values, so the equality case survives even though the valid `ep->f_shdr` indices are `0..3`. The function then computes `targpsh = ep->f_shdr + gseca` and immediately reads `targpsh->gh_section_group_number`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 at `dwarf_elf_load_headers.c:1790`. The fix changes these section-number checks from `>` to `>=`, blocking the exact `gseca == g_count` witness before the out-of-bounds dereference.

source.description: First project-side parse of vulnerability-relevant bound state. This line reads the attacker-controlled ELF header field `e_shnum` and materializes the total section count later used as the legal upper bound for section indices.
source.value_from: Static inspection of the staged `poc` with `readelf -h` reports `Number of section headers: 4`. This statement copies that attacker-controlled `e_shnum` into `ehdr->ge_shnum`, establishing the later valid section-index range `0..3`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Off-by-one section-index validation. Valid entries for `ep->f_shdr` are strictly less than `ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count`, but this code rejects only values strictly greater than that count. The exact witness equality case `gseca == ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count == 4` is therefore accepted and later used as a one-past-end array index.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes both section-number comparisons here from `>` to `>=`. On the witnessed bytes `04 00 00 00`, the primary decode already yields `gseca == 4`, so the `gsecb` fallback is not needed; the bug is that the equality case is treated as in range.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the accepted one-past-end pointer `ep->f_shdr + 4` is formed, this field read dereferences memory beyond the allocated `generic_shdr` array.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` here and says the faulting address is 128 bytes to the right of the 640-byte region allocated for the section-header array at line 553.

tainted_value_origin.description: This allocation creates the heap-backed `generic_shdr` array that later becomes `ep->f_shdr`. AddressSanitizer's allocation stack identifies this exact line as the origin of the 640-byte region that is read out of bounds.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: With the witness's parsed `count == 4`, this allocates four `generic_shdr` elements; the saved ASan trace reports the resulting region as `[0x616000000080, 0x616000000300)`.

parser_admitted.description: After libdwarf's object detector accepts the staged file as ELF and opens it, this call enters the non-libelf ELF parser path. The saved crash stack confirms that execution then reaches `_dwarf_load_elf_sectheaders()` and `_dwarf_elf_setup_all_section_groups()` on the crashing run.

fine_trace.note: Source. This line parses the attacker-controlled ELF header field `e_shnum`. For the staged witness it materializes `ehdr->ge_shnum == 4`, which later becomes the bound for the section-header array and defines the valid index range `0..3`.

Using the parsed section count from step 1, libdwarf allocates heap storage for four `generic_shdr` entries. This is the array later published as `ep->f_shdr`, and ASan names this exact line as the allocation context for the over-read region.

While decoding the witness's section-header table, these assignments materialize section header 1 as `SHT_GROUP` with payload offset `0x64`, size `0x0f`, and entry size `4`. Those fields determine that this section will be treated as a group-section payload and where its member list will be read from.

The decoded heap array from steps 2 and 3 is published as `ep->f_shdr`, and its authoritative bound becomes `ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count == 4`. Later validation and pointer arithmetic both use these exact fields.

The section-group setup loop walks the four decoded section headers. When it reaches section 1 from step 3, `elf_sht_groupsec(psh->gh_type,name)` recognizes `SHT_GROUP`, so execution bypasses the non-group `continue` path and enters `read_gs_section_group()` for that header.

For the witness's group section, `seclen == 0x0f` and `gh_entsize == 4`, so this derives `count == 3`. The existing pre-loop guard therefore stays false (`3 > 4` is false), which leaves the loop able to process the first group-member entry at `i == 1`.

After the 32-bit group flag, the first member bytes in the staged `poc` are `04 00 00 00` at file offset `0x68`. These lines copy and decode that entry into `gseca == 4`, the exact section number later used as an index.

Root cause. The witness makes `gseca == 4` and step 4 established `ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count == 4`, so the strict comparison `gseca > ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count` is false even though valid indices stop at 3. The code therefore accepts the one-too-large section reference instead of rejecting it as out of range.

Because step 8 did not reject the equality case, this pointer arithmetic uses `gseca == 4` against the four-element array from step 4. The result is a one-past-end `generic_shdr *` that does not name a real section header.

Sink. This field read dereferences the one-past-end pointer from step 9, producing the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8`. The sanitizer report places the fault 128 bytes past the 640-byte heap region allocated at step 2, which matches reading a field inside a non-existent fifth `generic_shdr` element.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: No fixed-version runtime confirmation was staged here, but the patch directly changes the witness-relevant comparisons from `>` to `>=`. For the exact witnessed value `gseca == ep->f_loc_shdr.g_count == 4`, that source-level change would raise `DW_DLE_ELF_SECTION_GROUP_ERROR` before `targpsh = ep->f_shdr + gseca` executes.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `default_crash_trace.txt`, `reproduction_report.json`, `patch.diff`, static inspection of the staged `poc`, and the vulnerable source snapshot under `gt_results/arvo_40674/_work/src/libdwarf`

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_40674 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/fuzz_init_path` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` in `read_gs_section_group`.

format.name: corrupted ELF64 object file with an SHT_GROUP section
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly the 1961-byte ELF64 big-endian file in `poc`. Static inspection shows `e_shnum == 4`; section header 1 is `SHT_GROUP` with `sh_offset == 0x64`, `sh_size == 0x0f`, and `sh_entsize == 4`; and the first 12 payload bytes at offset `0x64` are `01 00 00 00 04 00 00 00 13 00 00 00`. The source-grounded trigger established here is specifically that, after the 32-bit flag word, the first referenced section number decodes to exactly `4`, equal to the total section count, so the vulnerable `>` check treats a one-too-large section reference as in range. The staged evidence does not justify broadening this witness to arbitrary larger indices or unrelated malformed group layouts.
